outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Registration Certificate and Business Account Number (BAN). What to say: Apply online with the entity name, EIN and business description within 30 days of starting business. Fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, plus $4 state fee for 2026–27). The BAN is required for every other city permit (Planning, Health, Entertainment, DBI). File a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the entity name, publish it in a court-approved newspaper for four weeks, and file proof of publication within 45 days.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the building permit application with the Department of Building Inspection for tenant improvements, storefront merger and change of use, attaching the CUA approval and stamped architectural plans. What to say: Hire a California-licensed architect to prepare plans for the tenant improvements (storefront merger, bar layout, ADA restrooms, egress, soundproofing, lighting) and stamp them. Submit the building permit application online through DBI's permit tracking system with the BAN, the CUA approval (or a pending CUA case number if DBI allows pre-submittal), and the stamped plans. The application routes to Planning for zoning conformance review under § 175, and to other departments (DPH if any plumbing or sinks, Fire if sprinkler or hood work). Fees are a percentage of construction valuation (typically $800–$15,000 for a bar TI). Electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits are pulled by licensed subcontractors. Plan for 14–120 days depending on plan completeness and the scope of work. Schedule the final inspection after construction and before opening; DBI will not issue a certificate of occupan…

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 210 to 630 days. Estimated government cost: $7,633 to $35,450. Notes: The day and cost ranges cover the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000), Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800), health permit to operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000 for FY2026–27), and building permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000). The ranges are times to approval, not to denial or withdrawal. The CUA is the long pole (6–10 months including pre-application, environmental review, neighborhood notice and hearing scheduling). The cost does not include the ABC license: a Type 42 beer/wine bar is approximately $1,000–$1,600 in ABC fees and takes 60–150 days; a Type 48 full-liquor bar is typically purchased for $100,000–$450,000 (license purchase price plus transfer fees) and takes 90–240 days including escrow. Undue concentration in the census tract (46 ABC licenses within 1,000 ft) may add 1–3 months if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required. The figures do not include soft costs (architect, acoustic consultant, legal, broker), construction (tenant improvements to merge storefronts, soundproofing, ADA, bar build-out), or pre-opening operating expenses during the entitlement period.
